column1: What does ZeRO Stage 1 shard vs Stage 3?
column2: Stage 1 shards optimizer states only. Stage 3 shards parameters, gradients, and optimizer states.

column1: Why is TP restricted to within a NVLink node?
column2: TP requires synchronous all-reduce per layer — ~0.5ms on NVLink (900 GB/s) but ~160ms on 100 Gb/s InfiniBand. Cross-node TP latency destroys throughput.

column1: What does FSDP all-gather before each layer's forward pass?
column2: The full parameter shard for that layer from all GPUs in the DP group, reconstructing the layer's weights locally.

column1: What is the total memory cost (bytes per parameter) of AdamW training in BF16 with FP32 optimizer states?
column2: Roughly 16 bytes/parameter: 2 (BF16 weights) + 4 (FP32 master) + 4 (Adam m) + 4 (Adam v) + 2 (BF16 gradient) = 16.

column1: What does the 1F1B pipeline schedule minimize?
column2: The pipeline bubble (fraction of time GPUs are idle), reducing it to approximately 1/num_microbatches.
Tensor parallelism (within node) × Pipeline parallelism (across nodes) × Data parallelism (across replicas).

column1: What is expert parallelism (EP) and when is it needed?
column2: EP assigns MoE experts to specific GPUs and routes tokens accordingly. Needed for large MoE models (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-MoE) where expert count exceeds per-node GPU memory.

column1: How does gradient checkpointing trade compute for memory?
column2: It discards intermediate activations during the forward pass and recomputes them during backward, reducing activation memory ~3× at ~30% extra compute cost.

column1: What is the communication pattern in standard DDP vs FSDP?
column2: DDP: all-reduce gradients after each backward (one communication round). FSDP: all-gather parameters before forward, reduce-scatter gradients after backward (two communication rounds per layer, but smaller per-device memory).
